paragraphs: R. Chananyah, deputy of the priests: Avot, chapter 3. In the Mishnah: Pesachim 1:6, 14a; Shekalim 4:4, 6:1; Eduyot 2:1, 2, where the name is Chanina; Zevachim 9:3, 84a, and 12:4; Menachot 10:1; Bekhorot 6:3, 4, 10, 11 and 7:2, 5 [all six retrieved passages name R. Chanina ben Antigonos]; Negaim 1:4; Parah 3:1. He said a law in his father's name. End of chapter 1 of Yoma, 21b: he said he saw fire on the altar crouching like a dog. He also lived after the destruction, since he disagrees with R. Meir and R. Yosi: Yoma, chapter 1, 8a, “R. Chanina, deputy of the priests, says, etc.”; beginning of chapter 4, 39a, R. Chanina the deputy. This requires investigation, since he was killed at the destruction. He was killed on 25 Sivan with Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel and R. Yishmael: Shulchan Arukh, Orach Chayyim, section 580. Jerusalem Pesachim, chapter 1, halakhah 6, places him before Usha; see Rabban Gamliel the Elder above. It is known that Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel was killed at the destruction; thus Usha was after the destruction. Peer Halakhah writes: Rambam ruled like R. Chanina the deputy that surplus libation funds go toward supplementary offerings on the altar, against R. Akiva, who disagrees in Shekalim, chapter 4. Kesef Mishneh asked: does the law not follow R. Akiva against his colleague? He suggested that R. Chanina the deputy presumably knew more about Temple matters. The aforementioned book challenges Kesef Mishneh's answer. R. Yochanan ben Zakkai was his colleague; see there. His son was R. Shimon ben HaSegan; see there.
